POP zebra wall

The upper stripe heads are irregular and mostly upright. The broad left sweep and curved right bands follow the photo. Exact brushwork and the warm spill from the reference fixtures are approximate.

BeforeAfter

Wall artwork and packed UVs

The first image you shared is organized in wall order. The second is the previous packed atlas. Each new island samples the same wall artwork, including 12 pixels of padding across its edges.

The exposed strips use 280 texels per metre in both directions. The patch behind the collage uses 96. Independent ray tests from seven review eyes found 62.2% potentially visible atlas coverage, up from 48.7% in the seamless planar trial. Black paint sampled by the wall is included in these figures. Four fixed views and a 25-position aisle sweep showed continuous stripe edges. At the old joins, 8,522 exposed near-edge samples showed zero hard black-to-cream jumps. Extreme close-ups still show slight differences in stripe-edge softness.

Shutter-side alcove

The teal panel beside the Halo Dirty shutter now has distinct, staggered stipple at the marked camera distance. Its 1024-square fold uses the same continuous pattern on both sides. The neighboring framed picture uses a 230 × 240 original crop, which limits its recoverable detail.

BeforeAfter

Wavy counter

The wavy counter recovers photographed brush detail from the original 1152-square paint source. The existing 4096-square shared atlas is retained. A restrained baked reflection gives the resin more sheen. The red drink wells and zebra fascia keep their original finishes.

Ceiling and patio

The included viewer starts with the Hall and POP ceilings hidden. Show ceiling restores their overhead pieces, including the POP flags, ivy and chandelier. The two side patio planters by the picnic tables received localized baked fill.

Flicker checks

Each test used 153 saved viewpoints with the ceiling hidden, the same 153 with it shown, and 240 exterior views at two heights. At each fixed camera the draw-order test exposed adjacent surfaces that switched pixels.

Values count pixels with a change above 22 on at least one 8-bit RGB channel, rendered at 600 × 400. 78 of 546 fitted combinations had at least one threshold hit, with a maximum of 18 pixels. The wide-range stress test retained more edge and clipping differences at grazing angles.

Coverage and limits

The final model was rendered across the Main Hall, East and West bars, POP, covered aisle, patio, exterior and doorways. The gallery presents selected room, cutaway and orbit views from the same export.

Material and texture inventory

85 of 85 materials use the unlit glTF extension. Lighting and worktop sheen are baked into the appearance. This export has no live roughness, metalness, normal maps, or view-dependent reflections. The atlas channels, vertex colors and texture sizes below were read directly from the GLB.
